claims.claim: SpaceX's Raptor engine uses a full-flow staged combustion cycle with both oxidizer-rich and fuel-rich preburners, flowing all propellant through the turbines.
claims.episode_span: The engine uses a full-flow staged-combustion cycle in which both fuel-rich and oxidizer-rich preburners drive separate turbopumps before all propellant flows through the main chamber.
claims.supporting_quote: This type of combustion is a twin-shaft staged combustion cycle that uses both oxidizer-rich and fuel-rich preburners. The cycle allows for the full flow of both propellants through the turbines without dumping any unburnt propellant overboard.

claims.claim: Raptor operates at chamber pressures above 250 bar; the first version targeted 250 bar and 300 bar was reached in testing by July 2022.
claims.episode_span: allowing chamber pressures above 250 bar and specific impulse values competitive with far more exotic propellants
claims.supporting_quote: The first version was intended to operate at a chamber pressure of 250 bars (25 MPa; 3,600 psi) . [ 49 ] As of July 2022, chamber pressure had reached 300 bars in a test.

claims.claim: Methane was selected for Raptor partly because it can be synthesized on Mars from local carbon dioxide and water via the Sabatier reaction.
claims.episode_span: Methane and oxygen were selected because they can be produced on Mars from local resources
claims.supporting_quote: Because of the presence of underground water and carbon dioxide in Mars atmosphere , methane, a simple hydrocarbon , could be synthesized on Mars using the Sabatier reaction .

claims.claim: Methane/liquid-oxygen propellant reduces the coking and soot deposition on engine components that kerosene produces.
claims.episode_span: because methane avoids the coking that kerosene leaves on injector surfaces
claims.supporting_quote: a methane/ liquid oxygen combination offers the advantage over kerosene / liquid oxygen combination, or kerolox, of producing small exhaust molecules, reducing coking or deposition of soot on engine components.

claims.claim: SpaceX stated in 2019 that Raptor's marginal cost was approaching US$1 million with a mass-production target below US$250,000 per engine, and Raptor 2's production cost was described as roughly half that of Raptor 1 (mid-six figures).
claims.episode_span: Public statements and regulatory filings place early Raptor unit costs in the low millions; later versions are described in the same sources as having reached the mid-six-figure range, though exact current figures remain proprietary.
claims.supporting_quote: In 2019 the (marginal) cost of the engine was stated to be approaching US$1 million . SpaceX planned to mass-produce up to 500 Raptor engines per year, each costing less than US$250,000 .

claims.claim: The 'Idiot Index' — the ratio of a finished component's cost to the cost of its raw materials — is Elon Musk's term for the metric he uses to target overpriced parts.
claims.episode_span: Elon Musk later gave the two analytical tools their current shorthand names and applied them publicly to rockets and vehicles
claims.source_title: What I Learned About Manufacturing From Elon Musk
claims.supporting_quote: Elon also had an internal calibration helping guide cost that he called the ‘idiot index’. The idiot index measures how much a finished component costs compared to the raw materials.

claims.claim: Solar module prices have followed a learning curve for decades, declining about 20% with each doubling of global cumulative capacity.
claims.episode_span: The solar and semiconductor industries have followed the same pattern for sixty years, driving module and chip costs down curves measured in cents per watt or cents per transistor.
claims.source_title: Learning curve: Technologies that follow Wright’s Law - Our World in Data
claims.supporting_quote: For more than four decades, the price of solar panels declined by 20% with each doubling of global cumulative capacity.
